subject: Geography
description: Concept pool for UPSC Prelims — Geography > Physical Geography > Biogeography. Covers biomes, ecosystems, biodiversity, protected areas, wetlands, vegetation, and forest ecology as tested in UPSC Prelims 2014–2024. Each concept carries trap_affinity (which trap IDs historically apply), links_to (cross-concept interlinkages for hard A/R questions), and ca_trigger_types (what current affairs events activate this concept as a UPSC question).

sub_concepts.topic: Tropical rainforest — equatorial location, high biodiversity, year-round rainfall
Savanna — tropical grassland with distinct wet and dry seasons, between equatorial and desert biomes
Taiga (boreal forest) — coniferous forest, cold winters, short summers, dominates Canada/Russia
Tundra — treeless, permafrost, Arctic/alpine, mosses and lichens dominant
Temperate deciduous forest — seasonal leaf shedding, moderate rainfall, broadleaved trees
Mediterranean shrubland (chaparral) — dry hot summers, mild wet winters, fire-adapted vegetation
India's four biodiversity hotspots — Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma, Sundaland
Hotspot criteria — must have ≥1500 endemic vascular plant species AND ≥70% habitat loss
Western Ghats — overlap with multiple states, rich endemic amphibians/reptiles
Eastern Himalayas hotspot — includes NE India, Bhutan, SW China; distinct from Indo-Burma
Global hotspot count — 36 recognized hotspots covering ~2.4% of Earth's land area but >50% of endemic species

Biotic vs abiotic components — organisms vs physical/chemical environment interactions

Wetland ecosystems — transition zones between aquatic and terrestrial, high productivity

sub_concepts.topic: 10% energy transfer rule (Lindemann's law) — only 10% energy transferred between trophic levels
Trophic level hierarchy — producers (Level 1), primary consumers, secondary, tertiary consumers
Grazing food chain vs detritus food chain — different energy pathways
Ecological pyramids — pyramid of numbers, biomass, energy; inverted pyramid cases
Bioaccumulation and biomagnification — concentration increases up trophic levels (DDT, mercury)
Primary succession — starts on bare substrate (rock, sand, lava), pioneer community to climax
Secondary succession — starts on disturbed but soil-bearing land, faster than primary
Climax community — stable self-perpetuating community; type depends on climate
Hydrosere — aquatic succession from open water to marsh to terrestrial climax
Xerosere — succession in dry/arid conditions; lithosere as subtype on bare rock

sub_concepts.topic: Tropical evergreen forest — rainfall >200 cm, West Coast, NE India, dense multilayer canopy, no distinct dry season
Tropical moist deciduous — monsoon forests, teak dominant, 100–200 cm rainfall zone
Tropical dry deciduous — 70–100 cm rainfall, broader distribution in Deccan interior, sal and teak
Thorny scrub/arid vegetation — <70 cm rainfall, Rajasthan, acacia, cactus-like plants
Montane forests — altitudinal zonation: temperate forests → subalpine → alpine pastures in Himalayas
Mangrove forests — tidal inundation zones, delta coasts, Sundarbans as largest in India

sub_concepts.topic: Alluvial soil — Indo-Gangetic plains, khadar (new) vs bangar (old), most fertile, deposited by rivers
Black cotton soil (Regur) — volcanic Deccan plateau, expansive when wet, ideal for cotton
Red and yellow soil — iron oxide presence, Eastern India, less fertile than alluvial
Laterite soil — high rainfall leached of silica, leaves iron/aluminium oxides, Western Ghats, not good for crops
Arid/desert soil — sandy, low organic content, saline patches, Rajasthan
Soil horizon development (O-A-B-C) and pedogenic processes in different climates

ca_trigger_types: crop failure due to soil issues

sub_concepts.topic: National Park — highest protection, no human activity or settlement inside, boundary fixed by legislation
Wildlife Sanctuary — allows some human activity, boundary modifiable by state govt, less restrictive than NP
Biosphere Reserve — UNESCO MAB programme, three zones (core, buffer, transition), people allowed in outer zones
Community Reserve and Conservation Reserve — lower categories, community involvement, Section 36 WPA
Eco-sensitive zones (ESZ) — buffer around protected areas, development restrictions

Critically Endangered species of India — Great Indian Bustard, Hangul, Asiatic Cheetah (EW), Gharial
CITES Appendices — Appendix I (ban on commercial trade), II (regulated trade), III (national protection)
Endemic vs indigenous vs exotic — species origin and distribution categories
In-situ vs ex-situ conservation — protected areas vs zoos/seed banks/botanical gardens

sub_concepts.topic: Ramsar Convention — 1971, Ramsar Iran, 'Convention on Wetlands of International Importance'
Ramsar designation criteria — 9 criteria including >20,000 waterfowl support, 1% of species population
India's major Ramsar sites — Chilika Lake (Odisha), Keoladeo (Rajasthan), Loktak Lake (Manipur), Sundarbans
Wetland ecosystem functions — carbon sequestration, flood buffering, water purification, nutrient cycling
Montreux Record — list of Ramsar sites under threat needing priority conservation attention

sub_concepts.topic: Mangrove distribution — tidal inundation coasts, deltas, tropical/subtropical, not rocky coasts
Sundarbans — world's largest mangrove, India-Bangladesh shared delta, Royal Bengal Tiger habitat
Mangrove ecological functions — coastal protection, nursery habitat for fish, blue carbon storage
Mangrove adaptations — prop roots (Rhizophora), pneumatophores (Avicennia), viviparous germination
India's mangrove coasts — West Bengal (Sundarbans) largest; Andaman and Gujarat also significant
Coral bleaching — thermal stress causes expulsion of zooxanthellae algae, resulting in white appearance
Coral reef types — fringing, barrier, atoll; formation and position relative to coast
Coral reef distribution — warm shallow tropical waters, 23.5°N-23.5°S, India's reefs: Lakshadweep, Andaman, Gulf of Mannar
Zooxanthellae — symbiotic algae providing 90% of coral's energy via photosynthesis
Ocean acidification impact on coral — CO2 dissolves to form carbonic acid, reduces carbonate for skeleton
Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) — native to South America, invasive in India's freshwater bodies
Lantana camara — native to Central/South America, invasive in Indian forests, displaces native vegetation
Parthenium hysterophorus (congress grass) — native to Americas, allergen, impacts biodiversity
Common Myna and Rose-ringed Parakeet — invasive birds in urban India affecting native species
Island biogeography and invasion risk — islands more vulnerable to invasive species than mainland

sub_concepts.topic: Project Tiger — launched 1973, core-buffer zone approach, National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)
Tiger census methodology — camera trapping, pugmark, landscape-scale estimates every 4 years
Specific tiger reserves — Jim Corbett (first, Uttarakhand), Sundarbans, Ranthambore, Kaziranga, Nagarhole
Tiger reserve overlap with protected area types — core = NP/WLS, buffer = can include community land
India's tiger population recovery — from 1827 (2014) to 3682 (2022), ~70% of world's tigers

Social forestry — planting on community/non-forest land (roadsides, degraded areas) for local use
Agroforestry — integrating trees with crops/livestock; multilayer, improved soil, reduced runoff
Joint Forest Management (JFM) — community-state partnership for forest protection and benefit sharing

sub_concepts.topic: India's forest cover — FSI biennial assessment, ~21-22% of geographical area (ISFR 2021)
Forest types by density — Very Dense Forest (>70% canopy), Moderately Dense (40–70%), Open Forest (10–40%)
Deforestation drivers — agriculture expansion, logging, infrastructure, mining; differs by region
REDD+ mechanism — reducing emissions from deforestation in developing countries; UNFCCC framework
Carbon stock in forests — tropical forests store more carbon than temperate; peatlands as huge carbon sink

Central Asian Flyway — migratory bird route through India; key wetlands as stop-over points
Olive Ridley turtles — mass nesting (Arribada) on Odisha coasts, Gahirmatha Beach
